doc: S4: a worker whose folder is in project alpha calls plan_write on a plan of project beta (naming the task done) and on a plan of its own project alpha. Beta's plan keeps its task's title and status; alpha's takes the change (so the calls reached the hub). Another job's tasks, which have no project, are the unit test an_agent_reaches_its_own_jobs_tasks_only: a plan needs a project, so no row can name one. What makes it fail: a scope that lets an agent name any plan id.

args: mkdir -p $ROOT/work/alpha && cd $ROOT/work/alpha && export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='@1700000000 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='@1700000000 +0000' && git -c init.defaultBranch=main init -q && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q --allow-empty -m alpha

mkdir -p $ROOT/work/beta && cd $ROOT/work/beta && export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='@1700000100 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='@1700000100 +0000' && git -c init.defaultBranch=main init -q && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q --allow-empty -m beta

sql: select id from entity where kind = 'project' order by n
select title, status from entity where title in ('a task', 'a edited', 'b task', 'hacked') order by title
